diffs.diff: chip ID register 0x7: part 33220, datasheet reading 50305
diffs.evidence: Both readings describe the same register; only the byte encoding differs. Vishay VEML7700 datasheet (doc 84286), Command Code #7: 'The low byte of the ID register contains the device specific ID code 81h. The high byte contains ... 0xC4 for a device with slave address 0x20' (Table 8: bits 15:8 = 0xC4, bits 7:0 = 0x81), so the logical 16-bit value is 0xC481 = 50305. The I2C read protocol in the same datasheet is 'S, Slave address, Wr, A, Command code, A, S, Slave address, Rd, A, Data byte (LSB), A, Data byte (MSB), N, P', so the bytes on the wire are 0x81 then 0xC4. The simulator's 16-bit register store (src/sim/devices.ts setReg) always sends the high byte of the stored value first ([(v>>8)&0xff, v&0xff]) and has no per-register little-endian option. To make it send 0x81 then 0xC4, the model has to store 0x81C4 = 33220. The 0x00 entry follows the same rule: 256 = 0x0100 sends 0x01, 0x00, which is the datasheet power-on default ALS_CONF = 0x0001 (ALS_SD = 1, shut down). The driver reads d[0] | d[1] << 8, which gives 0xC481, and checks that the low byte is 0x81, as the datasheet says. SKILL.md gives low byte 0x81 and high byte 0xC4. The model's value is the correct wire-order encoding of the datasheet ID, and no change is needed.
